title: Mail: multi-MIME, inline quote, duplicate Message-ID, ancestors and missing references
annotator: claude-sonnet-5.5 worker, hand annotation on 2026-10-24 (hand-reading by a language model; no human review; no program produced any expected value)
independence_statement: Message bodies are short synthetic texts written by the language model annotator. Contributed text, quoted text, ancestor lists and missing references were decided by a language model reading each body closely. No parser, grouping code or A2 code was run or imported.

sources: ADDED CASES P06 to P09, N07, N08 (independent follow-up for review finding M2): hand-written by a language model (Claude Sonnet 5.5 worker) from docs/notes/parser-mime-html.md (transfer decoding, attachment subtree, structural and transfer defects become generic limitations) and docs/notes/parser-qualification.md (MIME row). No program produced any value. T0-02-P08 is PROPOSED: the A1 note is silent on an empty MIME leaf and the value needs owner sign-off.
docs/notes/preparation-semantics.md: 'Grouping relationship conventions' (in_reply_to, outlook_conversation, missing parent, cycles)
docs/notes/parser-mime-html.md: part references 1, 1.1, 1.2; inline and attachment handling
docs/notes/parser-qualification.md: MIME row (quoted-printable alternatives, multipart relationships, base64 attachment)
tests/outlook_mail_handoff_fixtures.py (A1 accepted mail fixture shapes, read only)

A2-LEVEL DECISION, NOT FROM A1 DOCS: the split of a reply body into contributed text and quoted text (P02, P03, N04) and the oldest-first ancestor order (P03) are task-level annotations. The cited A1 docs do not define them. They need owner sign-off like any A2 rule.

Scope and parent presence in P02, P03 and P04 follow docs/notes/preparation-semantics.md 'Grouping relationship conventions': a record carries exactly one source_scope, and an exact present parent with the same scope can confirm membership.

cases.title: References names a message that is not in the catalog

cases.title: Attachment part is separate from the body contribution
Quoted-printable UTF-8 text part is transfer-decoded, including a soft line break

parts.raw:
Review the caf=C3=A9 plan to=
day.

cases.rationale: docs/notes/parser-mime-html.md: readable text and HTML leaves are 'transfer-decoded and decoded with their declared character set'. docs/notes/parser-qualification.md MIME row names quoted-printable UTF-8. The decoded string was derived by hand: =C3=A9 is the UTF-8 pair for the letter e with acute accent, and '=' at the end of a line joins the lines.

cases.title: Base64 text part is transfer-decoded and the encoded form is not kept as text
cases.rationale: Same A1 sentence as P06. The base64 text SGVsbG8gV29ybGQh decodes to Hello World! (decoded manually, 12 bytes in four groups of three).

cases.title: Empty plain-text body gives an empty contribution, not an error and not invented text
cases.rationale: PROPOSED. The A1 MIME note names an empty-content limitation only for direct TEXT, HTML and JSON inputs, not for an empty MIME leaf. The A1 text is silent here. The value is the plain safe answer: keep the record, add no text.

cases.title: Attached message/rfc822: the inner message is metadata, not body text
cases.rationale: docs/notes/parser-mime-html.md: 'Attachment disposition applies to the complete subtree ... no readable descendant is emitted as message-body text. This includes attached message/rfc822 and multipart containers.' The ref 1.2.1 follows the nested numbering rule in the same note.

cases.title: Duplicate Message-ID with different bodies must not be merged or silently deduplicated

records.text: A different body with the same id.

expected.reason: ambiguous identity: one Message-ID, two distinct source versions

cases.rationale: Records are identified by exact VersionRef, not by Message-ID. A reply that points to <dup@...> has two possible parents, which is ambiguous, not confirmed.

cases.title: Reply pointing at an ambiguous duplicate parent is not confirmed
Equal subjects never create a group
cases.rationale: Preparation semantics: grouping never reads subject text.
